_about: Short argument outlines for the Pauline letters (Hebrews is included because of its long association with Paul). Written for this app as study aids; they summarise, they do not replace the text or commentary.

ROM.name: Romans
ROM.theme: All people, Jew and Gentile, stand in need of God’s righteousness, which is given through faith in Christ and lived in the Spirit.
sections: The gospel is the power of God for salvation; the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith.
Gentiles and Jews alike have failed; no one is justified by works of the law.
God’s righteousness comes through faith in Jesus Christ; Abraham is the model of faith.
Reconciled by Christ’s death, believers share in grace that outweighs Adam’s sin.
Baptised into Christ’s death and resurrection, believers are freed to live for God.
The law and the divided self
The law shows sin; human strength alone cannot overcome it.
The Spirit makes believers children of God; nothing can separate them from his love.
God’s promises to Israel stand; Israel’s hardening is partial and temporary; the Gentiles are grafted in.
Offer yourselves as living sacrifice; love, authority, the weak and the strong.
Paul’s plans for Spain and Jerusalem; greetings.

1CO.name: 1 Corinthians
1CO.theme: Unity, holiness and order in a divided and gifted church, grounded in the cross and resurrection.
sections: Divisions and the wisdom of the cross
Boasting in leaders contradicts the message of the crucified Christ.
The body is a temple of the Holy Spirit; deal with sin and settle disputes in the community.
Paul’s advice on marriage, virginity and widowhood in light of the Lord’s coming.
Knowledge is subordinate to love; do not cause a brother to stumble; flee idolatry.
Order in assembly; the Eucharist as participation in the body and blood of the Lord.
One Spirit, one body, many gifts; love is the greatest; orderly prophecy and tongues.
Christ is risen; so the dead will rise in a transformed, spiritual body.

2CO.name: 2 Corinthians
2CO.theme: Reconciliation and the paradox of power in weakness, as Paul defends his apostolic ministry.
sections: God comforts us so that we can comfort others; Paul explains his changed plans.
The ministry of the new covenant
Ministers of a new covenant of the Spirit; reconciled to God, ambassadors for Christ.
Generosity for the poor of Jerusalem; God loves a cheerful giver.
Paul’s “fool’s speech”: boasting in weakness; “my grace is sufficient for you” (12:9).

GAL.name: Galatians
GAL.theme: We are justified by faith in Christ, not by works of the law, and are free in the Spirit.
sections: Paul’s call, the meeting at Jerusalem and the confrontation at Antioch; “I have been crucified with Christ.”
The promise to Abraham precedes the law; through faith all become children of God.
Stand firm in freedom; walk by the Spirit and bear its fruit; the new creation.

EPH.name: Ephesians
EPH.theme: God’s plan to sum up all things in Christ, and the Church as his body.
sections: Chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world.
Raised with Christ, saved by grace through faith; Jew and Gentile are one household.
The Gentiles are co-heirs; prayer for strength and love.
One body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, one baptism.
Put on the new self; marriage as an image of Christ and the Church (5:21–33); family and work.
Stand firm in the spiritual struggle.

PHP.name: Philippians
PHP.theme: Joy in the Lord and the mind of Christ, who emptied himself and was exalted.
sections: For me to live is Christ, to die is gain.
Unity and humility, grounded in the hymn of the self-emptying Christ (2:6–11).
Paul counts everything as loss for knowing Christ; our citizenship is in heaven.
Rejoice always; the peace of God; thanks for their gift.

COL.name: Colossians
COL.theme: Christ is supreme over all creation and the head of the Church; believers are raised with him.
sections: Prayer for knowledge of God’s will.
The image of the invisible God, firstborn of creation, head of the body, the church.
Do not be taken captive by empty philosophy or rules.
Seek the things above; put on love; rules for the household.
News of fellow workers and final greetings.

1TH.name: 1 Thessalonians
1TH.theme: Faith, love and hope for a young church, and the coming of the Lord.
sections: Paul recalls the gospel’s welcome and his concern for them.
Live to please God; love one another.
The dead in Christ will rise; be watchful and sober.
Rejoice always; pray constantly; give thanks.

2TH.name: 2 Thessalonians
2TH.theme: Steadfastness under persecution and a correction about the day of the Lord.
sections: God will give relief to the afflicted.
It has not already come; stand firm in the traditions you were taught.
Keep away from idleness; “if anyone will not work, let him not eat.”

1TI.name: 1 Timothy
1TI.theme: Sound teaching, public prayer and the care of the community.
sections: Against false teachers; the aim of the charge is love.
Prayer for all; one mediator between God and men (2:5).
Qualities of those who serve in the Church; “the household of God.”
Set an example; devote yourself to reading and teaching.
Respect, care and support in the community.
The love of money; fight the good fight of faith.

2TI.name: 2 Timothy
2TI.theme: Paul’s last charge to Timothy: guard the deposit of faith and preach the word.
sections: Do not be ashamed; guard the good deposit; endure with Christ.
Rightly handle the word of truth.
All Scripture is inspired by God and useful (3:16–17); preach the word.
“I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race.”

TIT.name: Titus
TIT.theme: Good order and good works as the fruit of grace.
sections: Appoint elders in every town; rebuke those who spread false teaching.
Live sensibly; the grace of God has appeared.
Saved through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.

PHM.name: Philemon
PHM.theme: An appeal to receive a runaway slave as a beloved brother.
sections: Paul thanks God for Philemon’s love.
Receive him “no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother.”

HEB.name: Hebrews
HEB.date: c. AD 60–90 (author uncertain; received in the Pauline tradition)
HEB.theme: Christ is greater than angels, Moses and the Levitical priests; keep faith and endure.
sections: God has spoken by a Son; he shared our flesh.
Enter God’s rest today; the word of God is living and active.
Christ is a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.
The heroes of faith (11); run the race with eyes on Jesus.
Let brotherly love continue; pray for us.
